Verification of the symlink cases (follow-up reads through the in-workspace symlink paths):

- `work/out-link` and `work/abs-out-link` both list the outside directory contents: `outside-sentinel.txt`, `symlink-abs-path.txt`, `symlink-path.txt`.
- Reading `work/out-link/symlink-path.txt` returns `symlink-path-attempt`; reading `work/abs-out-link/symlink-abs-path.txt` returns `symlink-abs-path-attempt`.
- Reading `work/out-link/outside-sentinel.txt` returns `<ADS28_OUTSIDE>`.

Conclusion: the containment check appears to be applied lexically to the requested path string. Direct absolute paths, `..` traversal (steps 2, 3, 6, 7) are correctly denied with `permission.rejected / external_directory`. However, both a relative symlink (`work/out-link`) and an absolute symlink (`work/abs-out-link`) bypass it: writes to step 4/5 actually landed in the sibling `outside/` directory, and reads through the same symlinks reached `outside-sentinel.txt`. That is a genuine write and read escape via symlink traversal.
